hunt.justification: ClickFix attacks bypass file-based defenses by utilizing user interaction to execute signed system binaries. Confirming the absence of this behavior ensures the estate is resilient to this high-velocity social engineering campaign.

stages.name: Social Engineering via Run Dialog
observables: Process command line containing cmd.exe /c start "" /min
Caret obfuscation in command line (e.g., s^t^a^r^t, f^^i^^n^^g^^e^^r)
Social engineering strings in command line (e.g., ---P_u_s_h----t_h_e----_E_n_t_e_r_----k_e_y--)
Command line containing 'for /f' loops to execute captured text

stages.name: LOLBIN Payload Retrieval
observables: finger.exe used within a 'for' loop to capture and execute output

scenario.summary: ClickFix is a social engineering campaign that tricks users into pasting obfuscated commands into the Windows Run dialog, which are then executed by explorer.exe. These commands leverage native LOLBINs like finger.exe to download and execute follow-on payloads such as infostealers without writing files to disk.

meta.rationale: Scope focuses on Windows endpoints where users interact with the Run dialog. Explorer.exe parentage is the primary scoping mechanism within behavioral telemetry.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder is using social engineering to trick users into pasting obfuscated commands into the Windows Run dialog, using explorer.exe to launch downloaders like finger.exe for payload retrieval.

hunt.name: ClickFix Run-Dialog Social Engineering and LOLBIN Execution
hunt.description: ClickFix attacks bypass traditional file-based defenses by delivering commands directly into the user interactive session via the Windows Run dialog. The command usually contains caret obfuscation to defeat string matching and uses built-in Microsoft binaries like finger.exe to fetch and execute a remote payload. This hunt identifies the specific explorer.exe to cmd.exe or LOLBIN process relationship, detects the obfuscated command patterns, and stack-counts rare explorer children to separate legitimate activity from the attack.

coverage.reason: General hb_ surfaces do not track specific file-level access to browser sqlite databases required for high-fidelity credential theft detection.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%microsoft%' AND LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%windows%'
config.description: Identify Windows systems which are the primary target for ClickFix social engineering via the Run dialog.
config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames running Windows. This list is used to scope subsequent behavioral queries.

primitive_config.label: Scope to Windows endpoints
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%microsoft%' AND LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%windows%'
primitive_config.expected: A list of hostnames running Windows. This list is used to scope subsequent behavioral queries.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\explorer.exe' AND (process_cmd_line LIKE '%^%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%finger%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%for /f%' OR instr(',' || '{{social_eng_strings}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_cmd_line) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find instances where explorer.exe spawns cmd.exe or LOLBINs with caretaker obfuscation, finger usage, or social engineering strings.
config.expected_signal: A shell or system binary launched by explorer.exe containing caret characters, for-loops, or the social engineering padding. This is the primary lead.

primitive_config.label: Identify explorer-spawned obfuscated shells
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\explorer.exe' AND (process_cmd_line LIKE '%^%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%finger%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%for /f%' OR instr(',' || '{{social_eng_strings}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_cmd_line) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A shell or system binary launched by explorer.exe containing caret characters, for-loops, or the social engineering padding. This is the primary lead.

config.objective: Determine if the command lines in identify-obfuscated-launchers contain caretaker obfuscation, for/f loops used for execution, or long strings of dashes/social engineering instructions.
config.description: Analyze the command line for ClickFix characteristics like social engineering padding and download cradle logic.
config.expected_signal: A verdict on whether the command line represents a ClickFix lead.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict of suspicious | malicious | benign citing the command line rows.

config.question: the evaluate-launcher-logic verdict is suspicious or malicious for at least one host
config.condition: the evaluate-launcher-logic verdict is suspicious or malicious for at least one host
config.description: Only proceed to expensive prevalence and network queries if the lead shows ClickFix behavior.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_name) AS binary, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, COUNT(*) AS launches FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\explorer.exe' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1 HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC
config.description: Stack-count children of explorer.exe to find anomalous launchers across the fleet.
config.expected_signal: The binary name used in the ClickFix attack appearing on very few hosts compared to standard Windows activity.

primitive_config.label: Rare processes spawned by explorer
primitive_config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_name) AS binary, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, COUNT(*) AS launches FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\explorer.exe' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1 HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC
primitive_config.expected: The binary name used in the ClickFix attack appearing on very few hosts compared to standard Windows activity.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, time FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{c2_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Search for DNS lookups to domains associated with ClickFix payload delivery.
config.expected_signal: A hostname resolving linkeders infrastructure shortly after the explorer launcher event.

config.objective: Confirm if any host shows the complete ClickFix chain: explorer.exe spawning an obfuscated command, that command being rare in the environment, and follow-on DNS activity to linkeders infrastructure.
config.description: Synthesize the launcher lead, the rarity baseline, and the network indicators to confirm a successful intrusion.
config.expected_signal: A detailed malicious verdict linking the user paste to successful payload retrieval.
config.success_criteria: A final malicious verdict per host with a summary of the evidence chain and timing correlation.

config.question: the triage-full-chain verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.condition: the triage-full-chain verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.description: Direct the analyst to isolation for confirmed threats or review for ambiguous findings.
Halt the attack chain and prevent data exfiltration by the infostealer payload.
config.instructions: Isolate the host immediately. Revoke all active web and application sessions for the affected user, as infostealer payloads often harvest session tokens.

config.description: Inspect the host for persistence and stage-two payloads.
config.instructions: Review the full process tree around the identified launcher. Look for randomly named executables or scripts in %APPDATA% or %TEMP% that may represent the infostealer stage. Confirm browser profiles are intact and force user password resets.

config.description: Document the hunt outcome and any negative results.
config.instructions: Record the examined scope and findings. If ClickFix was not found, note that no users executed obfuscated cradles via explorer.exe in the lookback period.
